He's covered in about 6 million tiles, and some have secret messages on the back. ✝️ Watch Christ the Redeemer go up: 9 years in 28 seconds. ⏱️

700 m up on Corcovado. A reinforced-concrete figure engineered by Albert Caquot from Paul Landowski's design (he made the head and hands full size in clay in France). 30 m tall on an 8 m pedestal, arms 28 m wide. Then millions of small soapstone tiles were set by hand.

The twist: the tile workers wrote notes and names on the backs of tiles, so the statue carries hidden messages. And lightning keeps hitting it.

yt_title: How Christ the Redeemer Was Built: 9 Years in 28 Seconds #shorts
yt_description:
Built 1922–1931 on Corcovado (~700 m): designed by Heitor da Silva Costa with Carlos Oswald, sculpted by Paul Landowski (face by Gheorghe Leonida), reinforced-concrete structure by Albert Caquot; 30 m statue on an 8 m pedestal with a 28 m arm span, covered in about 6 million soapstone tiles. Tile workers wrote messages on the backs of tiles. Opened 12 Oct 1931; struck by lightning in 2008 and 2014.

Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christ_the_Redeemer_(statue) · https://www.mentalfloss.com/article/84546/11-facts-about-rios-christ-redeemer-statue · https://www.thecollector.com/who-made-the-statue-of-christ-the-redeemer
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
